Under Law 12, the goalkeeper commits an offence by handling the ball inside their own penalty area after it has been deliberately kicked to them by a team-mate, and this is penalised with an indirect free kick to Red. The kick is taken from where the offence occurred, subject to Law 13 (if within the goal area, from the goal area line parallel to the goal line at the nearest point). No caution is required because no goal or obvious goal-scoring opportunity was denied.

Under Law 12, a goalkeeper may not handle the ball inside their own penalty area after it has been deliberately kicked to them by a team-mate, so an indirect free kick is awarded to Red where the goalkeeper touched the ball. If that spot is inside the goal area, the kick is taken from the nearest point on the goal area line parallel to the goal line (Law 13). No sanction is required because no goal-scoring opportunity was denied.

Under Law 12, the goalkeeper commits an offence by handling the ball inside their own penalty area after it has been deliberately kicked to them by a teammate. Under Law 11, a player in an offside position who receives the ball from an opponent who deliberately played it (other than a deliberate save) is not considered to have gained an advantage. A miskick or poorly executed deliberate pass by the defender is still a deliberate play, so the Red forward is not penalised for offside and play continues.

Under Law 13 (and Law 9 regarding ball in play), once the free kick is taken and the ball clearly moves it is in play, and the kicker may not touch it again before another player does. Playing it a second time is an offence penalised by an indirect free kick to Blue from where the second touch occurred. No disciplinary sanction applies unless the touch was otherwise a cautionable offence.

Under Law 13, once the free kick is taken and the ball is in play (kicked and clearly moves), the kicker must not touch it again until another player has touched it. A second touch by the kicker is an offence, and an indirect free kick is awarded to Blue from where the second touch occurred. No sanction is required unless it is a deliberate handball or another misconduct offence.

Under Law 13 (and Law 9 for restarts), once the free kick is taken and the ball is in play, the kicker must not touch it again before another player has touched it. The second touch is an offence, so an indirect free kick is awarded to Blue from where it occurred, with no sanction unless it stopped a promising attack or similar.

Under Law 14, after taking a penalty kick the kicker must not touch the ball again until it has touched another player; rebounding off the post does not count.
